chief_complaint: fever, back pain, and leg weakness
hpi_details: 65F presents with 3 weeks of worsening mid-back pain, low-grade fevers, and new-onset weakness and numbness in her bilateral lower extremities. She has a history of poorly controlled diabetes.

investigation_events.title: STAT contrast-enhanced spine MRI
investigation_events.availability_message: The STAT spine MRI is now available; blood cultures, empiric antibiotics, and neurosurgical consultation should not be delayed.

results.test: Contrast-enhanced thoracic and lumbar spine MRI
results.value: Posterior epidural rim-enhancing collection from T7 through T10 causing severe thecal-sac compression and cord edema

core_concepts: Triad of fever, spinal pain, and neurologic deficits.
common_misconceptions: Treating only as musculoskeletal back pain because fever might be mild.
dangerous_errors: Discharging patients with new neuro deficits without an urgent MRI.
management_principles: STAT full-spine MRI with contrast, blood cultures, empiric antibiotics, emergent neurosurgical consult.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) Clinical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 65F with worsening back pain, fever, and new leg weakness.
reference_soap.objective: Point tenderness over thoracic spine. 4/5 strength in bilateral lower extremities. Decreased sensation below umbilicus.
reference_soap.plan: STAT MRI thoracic/lumbar spine with contrast. Neurosurgery consult. Blood cultures, then IV Vancomycin and Ceftriaxone.

learning_objectives: Identify the triad of spinal epidural abscess and order urgent MRI.

teaching.one_liner: Fever, localized back pain, and progressive neurologic deficits (leg weakness) necessitating urgent MRI.

must_ask.say: Where exactly is the back pain, and is it constant or does it come and go?
Have you had any fevers over the past few weeks?
Have you noticed any weakness or numbness in your legs?
Have you had any trouble controlling your bladder or bowels?
Do you have diabetes, or any recent infections, injections, or IV drug use?
